root_cause: The BackupScheduler bound to the old key kept running while local data was wiped or the identity was switched. The unload after a Danger Zone wipe (visibilitychange -> immediate mark), a peer tab's reload on the account-changed notice, and attempts already in flight across an identity replace could snapshot wiped or foreign storage and publish it as the old account's relay backup. A stale attempt could also connectNdk(oldKey) and rebind the shared NDK signer.
fix: New lib/backup/suspension.ts: page-lifetime in-memory suspension + scheduler identity binding. resetAllData suspends first; the account-changed reload suspends before reloading. Suspension disposes the scheduler, makes markBackupDirty a no-op and drops pending marks. publishScheduledBackup bails out when stale (suspended or identity no longer bound) at entry and after every await. publishBackup checks a mayPublish guard as its very last step before the network publish; a dropped attempt keeps the dirty mark and is not retried. replaceIdentity detaches the binding before persisting a different identity (detachBackupForReplace); the new identity's scheduler binds on mount.

tests_added.kinds: suspension semantics (no mark, no replay, scheduler disposed, not persisted); real publishBackup with deferred relay discovery (suspend / identity replace mid-flight -> no network publish, mark kept); stale-attempt paths (no connectNdk(oldKey)); resetAllData and account-changed reload ordering; same-tab identity replace still backs up

mutation.survivors: equivalent: log strings, ok:false literal of a skipped result that nothing reads, optional chaining on a non-null scheduler

e2e.result: non-relay 72 passed; relay 352 passed, 19 skipped, 1 failed (AC-60 groups-dm-reactions: composer Enter press timed out after 30 s, before any reaction code ran; known undiagnosed load stall, filed as dm-composer-enter-press-hangs-30s); no INVALID marker. groups-dm-reactions rerun 5x in isolation on a fresh relay: 5/5 green (4/4 each).

retrospective.harder_than_needed: A guard 'right before publish' was first placed before two awaits (dynamic import + up to 8 s relay discovery); mocked publishBackup tests could not see it. Only a test driving the real publishBackup with deferred discovery proved placement.
retrospective.surprised_by: connectNdk(privateKeyHex) rebinds the shared NDK signer, so even a 'harmless' stale backup attempt silently switches the signer back to the old identity (same root as connectndk-rebinds-external-signer).
lead_clarifications: Chose suspension over an 'empty snapshot' heuristic (would block legitimately emptied accounts and needs remote state).
